WITH order_counts AS (
    SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) as order_count
    FROM "order"
    GROUP BY account_id
),
global_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(order_count) as avg_orders
    FROM order_counts
),
above_avg_accounts AS (
    SELECT oc.account_id, oc.order_count
    FROM order_counts oc
    WHERE oc.order_count > (SELECT avg_orders FROM global_avg)
),
kept_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(order_count) as avg_of_kept
    FROM above_avg_accounts
)
SELECT 
    aaa.account_id,
    aaa.order_count,
    aaa.order_count - (SELECT avg_orders FROM global_avg) as above_global_avg,
    aaa.order_count - (SELECT avg_of_kept FROM kept_avg) as above_kept_avg
FROM above_avg_accounts aaa
ORDER BY above_kept_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: All rows in the "order" table are treated as standing orders; the table does not distinguish standing orders from other order types, so we count all orders.
